# Lenz 0.0.24 beta

This release brings project tabs, Format Selection and a new welcome screen to Lenz Code (PR #75).

- **Project tabs.** One window or terminal holds several projects, each with its own folder, tabs, explorer, language servers and drafts. They show one at a time under a project strip, or **Projects Side by Side** as columns. New, Open Folder in, Close, Next and Previous Project Tab are in the command menus; Ctrl+Alt+] and Ctrl+Alt+[ switch tabs. The desktop strip shares the width, each tab named `project – ~/path/to/the/shown/file`.
- **Open Recent Project** is a finder: type to filter by name, path or checked-out git branch, each shown beside the project. Choosing a project while this tab has another one open asks whether to open it in This Tab or a New Project Tab; Ctrl+Enter goes straight to a new project tab.
- **Welcome screen.** The start screen is a centred column of Start items (Open Folder…, Open Folder in New Project Tab…, New File) and recent projects with their locations, in both the window and the terminal. The terminal's Open Folder prompt lists recent projects, then folder suggestions as you type, with Tab completion.
- **Format Selection** formats the selected JSON or XML in place, re-indented to its line, as one undo step. Ctrl+Alt+L runs it when the selection is well-formed JSON or XML, and formats the document otherwise. XML has a built-in formatter that changes only whitespace. A plain-text file holding JSON or XML formats as that when you ask; Save never guesses.
- **Line-wise Cut, Copy and Paste.** With only carets, Ctrl+X cuts each caret's line, Ctrl+C copies it, and lines taken that way paste back above the caret's line.
- **YAML with ERB** (Rails `config/database.yml` and the like) no longer reports errors for the tags. The tags are highlighted as ERB with Ruby inside, and the YAML after them keeps its structure, highlighting and folds. Language-server edits that would change a tag are refused, and Format on Save leaves such files as typed.
- **macOS shortcut labels.** The desktop app spells Ctrl as Cmd and Alt as Opt in menus, the welcome screen and Find Action. ⌘⌥L runs Format Document. Terminals keep Ctrl.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. Lenz Code was compared with 0.0.23 on the same Linux machine, alternating builds: launch to readable is unchanged (136 ms median, warm and fresh), and a window with ten tabs settles about 5 MiB higher (205 MiB against 199 MiB). The terminal's first content, input and memory figures stay within run-to-run variation. Side by Side with several projects, and repeated opening and closing of project tabs, were not measured. Native macOS interaction, including the new Cmd and Opt labels, remains unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.23](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.23...v0.0.24).
